facts.statement: Sanxiasaurus is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur named after the Three Gorges of the Yangtze River.
facts.quote: Sanxiasaurus (meaning "Sanxia lizard", after the Three Gorges, Chinese Sanxia, of the Yangtze River) is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur

facts.statement: The only known species of Sanxiasaurus is S. modaoxiensis.
facts.quote: The type and only species is S. modaoxiensis.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Sanxiasaurus consists of 55 postcranial bones including vertebrae, forelimbs, hindlimbs, and foot parts.
facts.quote: The holotype is a partial postcranial skeleton consisting of 55 bones including two cervical vertebrae, 11 dorsal vertebrae, 4 sacral vertebrae, 18 caudal vertebrae, both humeri, radii, and ulnas, partial right ilium, partial right ischium, both femora and tibiae, left fibula, 3 metatarsi and 4 phalanges.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Sanxiasaurus as a basal neornithischian, more derived than Lesothosaurus but less derived than Hexinlusaurus.
facts.quote: In a phylogenetic analysis, it was found to be a basal neornithischian, more derived than Lesothosaurus and less derived than Hexinlusaurus.

facts.statement: A fossil bed containing Sanxiasaurus remains was discovered in 2016 in Laojun Village, Yunyang County, by a team from the Chongqing Bureau of Geological and Mineral Resource Exploration and Development.
facts.quote: In 2016 a field team from the Chongqing Bureau of Geological and Mineral Resource Exploration and Development discovered a new fossil-bearing bed in the Xintiangou Formation of Laojun Village, Yunyang County.

facts.statement: The remains were formally described in 2019 by Chinese paleontologist Ning Li and colleagues as the new taxon Sanxiasaurus modaoxiensis.
facts.quote: These remains, CLGPR V00003, were described in 2019 as the holotype of the new taxon by Chinese palaeontologist Ning Li and colleagues: Sanxiasaurus modaoxiensis.

facts.statement: Sanxiasaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 180 to 170 million years ago, in the Aalenian to Toarcian stages.
facts.quote: The Xintiangou Formation lies between the younger Lower Shaximiao and older Ziliujing Formation, with preliminary Uranium-lead dating giving it an Aalenian to Toarcian age of between 180 and 170 million years ago, during the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: Sanxiasaurus is the oldest known neornithischian dinosaur from Asia.
facts.quote: The ornithischian was the first of its kind from this formation and would be the oldest yet known from Asia.

facts.statement: The genus name Sanxiasaurus refers to the Three Gorges of the Yangtze River, and the species name modaoxiensis refers to the Modaoxi tributary.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to Sanxia, the Three Gorges of the Yangtze River that covers the area where the taxon was found, while the species name refers to the Yangtze tributary Modaoxi.

facts.statement: A 2024 analysis by André Fonseca and colleagues recovered Sanxiasaurus as more derived than Agilisaurus, potentially placing it in a clade with Hexinlusaurus or leaving its position unresolved.
facts.quote: Sanxiasaurus was found in a similar position by the analysis of Brazilian palaeontologist André Fonseca and colleagues in 2024, where it was consistently recovered more derived than Agilisaurus and either in a clade with Hexinlusaurus or unresolved, making Agilisaurus the most primitive neornithischian.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Sanxiasaurus spans from 184.2 to 170.9 million years ago, covering the Toarcian to Aalenian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Aalenian (184.2 to 170.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus authority for Sanxiasaurus is listed as Li et al., 2021 in some sources, differing from the 2019 description date.
